subject: Priority lane throughput appendix request — BorealCloud
messages:
From: Sasha Foley <sasha.foley@borealcloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@borealcloud.com
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Priority lane throughput appendix request

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the Hosted Dedicated walkthrough last week. We ran an internal run through and have a concrete ask: BorealCloud needs an appendix to the Dedicated contract that defines a "priority lane" for our enterprise customers. High-level asks:

- A committed throughput guarantee for the reserved GPUs backing the lane (sustained throughput for steady-state peaks; prefer tokens/sec or requests/sec guidance).
- Explicit queueing/isolation behavior so high-priority requests never see head-of-line blocking from lower-priority batch work.
- Deterministic tail-latency target for short requests (seq len <= 256).
- Maintenance window policy, preemption notice, and credits formula if targets are missed.

We want specific SLI numbers to evaluate against our own SLA commitments. Please let me know what data you need from our side (models, typical seq length, expected QPS). If you have a short one-pager or draft appendix that details what Redwood can offer, that would help speed approval.

Also looping in Legal: legal@borealcloud.com.

Thanks,
Sasha Foley
Head of Platform
BorealCloud

[Attachment: usage_snapshot_jan.zip (contains sample traces)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Foley <sasha.foley@borealcloud.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priority lane throughput appendix request

Sasha —

Appreciate the clear asks. We can draft an appendix but need a few clarifications to size guarantees appropriately:

1) How do you want throughput expressed? (tokens/sec, requests/sec, or concurrency per model variant)
2) Typical sequence length and 95th/99th token counts during your peak windows.
3) Percent of your dedicated pool you expect to reserve for the priority lane vs. general tenant work.
4) Any hard tail-latency targets you must meet (e.g., 99.9th < 300ms).

Quick note — Redwood supports per-route QoS and priority queues that can be mapped to a logical lane. We also expose token-level latency and per-route KPIs in Console and via our metrics API. I attached a one-pager that outlines our priority-lane capabilities.

I'll loop in Ben (sales/commitments) and Lauren (account ops) to propose initial commercial/legal language once we have these details.

— Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_priority_lanes_onepager.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Foley <sasha.foley@borealcloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed appendix outline (initial)

Sasha —

Following Rishi's note, we've sketched an initial appendix for discussion (see attached). Highlights:

- Committed throughput: baseline defined as tokens/second per reserved GPU at seq_len=256, measured as a 5-minute rolling average during the customer's peak window.
- Isolation: Logical priority queue assigned to reserved GPUs; priority requests enter a low-batch, low-latency execution path. Lower-priority batch work is shunted to best-effort queues.
- Tail latency target: 99.9th percentile < 350ms for seq_len <= 256 under normal operating conditions (subject to model characteristics).
- Burst policy: burst capacity up to 25% of pool for short bursts (<= 10 minutes) if available; credits and throttles apply thereafter.
- Maintenance: monthly 2-hour maintenance window with 72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance with best-effort notices.
- Credits: pro-rata service credit formula tied to the duration and severity of SLO misses.

I attached a draft (v0.2) for legal review. If these items look acceptable we can convert to contract language and attach to the Dedicated agreement.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed_sla_appendix_v0.2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sasha Foley <sasha.foley@borealcloud.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed appendix outline (initial)

Ben/Rishi —

Thanks for the quick draft. A few notes from our side:

- For throughput, we prefer requests/sec per model endpoint (customers have very different tokenization) — if you can map tokens/sec to requests/sec based on model family that would be ideal.
- The proposed 99.9th < 350ms is close, but BorealCloud requires 99.9th < 300ms for seq_len <= 256 for our customer SLA tiers. Can Redwood get there with an explicit low-batch execution path?
- We need an on-call runbook and escalation path in the appendix (who to page, expected ack within 30 minutes for Sev 1 affecting priority lane).

Also sharing SecOps contact in case compliance wants to review: secops@borealcloud.com.

If you can update the draft with these items we'll fast-track internal sign-off.

— Sasha

Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Technical feasibility: priority lane + deterministic tail

Hi Sasha and team —

Short answer: feasible with constraints. Notes below and recommended pilot config.

Key tradeoffs
- Continuous batching increases throughput but can inflate tail latency. To hit 99.9th < 300ms we need an execution path that minimizes batching for the priority queue (i.e., low-batch, low-latency kernel selection).
- KV-cache and prefix caching help reduce tokens/sec pressure for chat-like traffic; ensure warm cache policy for priority endpoints.
- Quantization (e.g., int8) materially reduces latency variability but depends on model fidelity requirements.

Recommended pilot (4 weeks)
- Dedicated pool of 8 GPUs with a logical priority lane guaranteeing 70% of steady-state throughput and a 25% burst bucket.
- Limit priority requests to seq_len <= 256 and capped model family set (we'll test with Llama-3-8B and Llama-3-70B quantized variants).
- SLI targets: 95th throughput sustain (requests/sec) measured per 5-minute window; 99.9th latency < 300ms for short seq path (measured end-to-end).
- Observability: expose per-route metrics (requests/sec, token/sec, p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latencies), traces, and an alerting policy. We'll provide a runbook template that covers on-call paging, escalation windows, and rollback to fallback model variants.

I'll attach the runbook draft and a sample metric mapping. If BorealCloud agrees, we'll size the pool and schedule a two-week soak after rollout. Time-to-prod for the pilot is ~2 weeks from agreement (for provisioning, model onboarding, and calibration).

— Soojin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: priority_lane_runbook.md (md)]
